_doc: Gold set for the key-terms DOMAIN-SEMANTIC judge. correct = real extracted definitions (verified against the source); incorrect = curated definitions that are lexically plausible but semantically WRONG — a swapped concept, a reversed relationship, or the opposite meaning — the class lexical grounding and entailment cannot catch. Recall on the incorrect class is the load-bearing bar (a wrong definition the judge calls correct is the failure that must not pass). Labels verified against the source text (P6).

sources.where_roots: where_roots/Where Roots Bowen Theory Reside in the Brain - Michael Kerr - 2022-02-18_valid/Where Roots Bowen Theory Reside in the Brain - Michael Kerr - 2022-02-18_valid - formatted.md

cases.label: correct
cases.definition: Described by the formula DOS = EO + A, meaning differentiation of self equals emotional objectivity plus action. It is a concept from Bowen theory in which emotional objectivity allows for emotional neutrality, enabling a person to engage others in a relatively non-reactive way and to take action without violating the boundaries of others or allowing others to violate one's own boundaries.

cases.label: correct
cases.definition: A brain network that includes sites in the executive prefrontal cortex, a region known to have a role in sustained attention and working memory. It jumps into action once the salience network has been activated, marshaling the brain's resources to enable action if necessary, and has the job of keeping a person focused on what is relevant to their goals while ignoring distractions.

cases.label: correct
cases.definition: A concept used to describe cancer as a disease of cell differentiation rather than multiplication, in which full development of the organism is hampered. The speaker draws a parallel to Bowen theory, where differentiation of an individual is hampered as a consequence of the level of fusion between parent and offspring.

cases.label: correct
cases.definition: A model of the solar system that places the Sun at the center, with planets including Earth orbiting around it. First authored by Aristarchus, it went underground for approximately 2,000 years before being restored to credibility by Copernicus and later confirmed by Galileo and Newton.

cases.label: correct
cases.definition: A term used by the speaker to describe a fundamental change in a dominant framework of understanding. The shift from the geocentric to the heliocentric model is presented as an example of a paradigm shift that took approximately 2,000 years to occur and dominate public consciousness.

cases.label: correct
cases.definition: A phrase used by the presenter to describe a small but meaningful expression of individual autonomy or self-definition. It is applied in two instances: the client walking away from the psychiatric hospital on his own volition, and the client's firm refusal to pay his daughter's rent, both interpreted as signs of a preserved sense of self.

cases.label: correct
cases.definition: A psychiatric state described in the transcript as being 'pulled into their shell,' in which the person is very aware of everything going on around them but is unable to reach outside themselves and relate to others.

cases.label: incorrect
cases.definition: The process by which family members manage unresolved emotional attachment to their parents and siblings by reducing or cutting off emotional contact with them, moving away, and rarely going home.
cases.note: WRONG CONCEPT — this is emotional cutoff, not differentiation of self

cases.label: incorrect
cases.definition: A concept describing cancer as a disease of uncontrolled cell multiplication and division, in which cells reproduce too rapidly.
cases.note: REVERSED — the source says cancer is differentiation-failure, NOT multiplication

cases.note: OPPOSITE — homeostasis is the maintenance of stable internal order

cases.definition: A model of the solar system that places the Earth at the center, with the Sun, Moon, and planets all orbiting around it.

cases.label: incorrect

cases.definition: A hyperactive, agitated psychiatric state in which the person is disoriented and unaware of their surroundings, unable to recall the episode afterward.
cases.note: OPPOSITE — catatonia is aware-but-unable-to-relate, not agitated and unaware

cases.label: incorrect
cases.definition: A phrase describing the client's complete loss of individual autonomy, evidenced by his total dependence on others for decisions and his inability to assert any boundary.
cases.note: OPPOSITE — the nubbin of self is a preserved expression of autonomy, not its loss

cases.label: incorrect

cases.label: incorrect
cases.definition: Two identical subsystems within the brain's reward system that both produce pleasure, such that wanting something and liking it are one and the same experience.
cases.note: REVERSED — wanting and liking are DISTINCT subsystems, not identical

cases.label: incorrect
cases.definition: A core concept in Bowen theory expressed as the equation DOS equals emotional objectivity minus action, where action is subtracted from objectivity to reach differentiation.
cases.note: REVERSED FORMULA — DOS = EO + A, not EO − A
